issues.legal_issue: The need to establish an adult married and unemployed son independently in business can constitute a bona fide personal requirement for release of a shop.
material_facts: The landlady sought the shop to enable her married, unemployed son, who had children, to start an electrical goods and utensils business of his own.
The landlady had no other shop in which to establish her son.
The tenant conceded before the Supreme Court that the landlady’s need to establish her son was bona fide.
The Court held that the son could not be compelled to join his father’s goldsmith and money-lending business.
issues.conclusion: The landlady’s need to establish her son independently in business was bona fide.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 21(1)(a) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, a landlord may seek release of a tenanted building on the ground of bona fide personal need. The Court treated the desire to establish the landlady’s married, unemployed son in an independent business as a bona fide need. No earlier cases were relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.tenant_eviction_release_proceeding: A landlord seeks release of premises occupied by a tenant.
predicates.adult_married_unemployed_son_seeks_indep: The landlord’s adult married and unemployed son seeks to establish himself in an independent business.
predicates.landlord_lacks_other_suitable_shop: The landlord has no other suitable shop in which to establish the son.
predicates.landlord_personal_need_is_bona_fide: The landlord’s need to use the premises for the stated personal purpose is bona fide.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks release of tenanted premises, and an adult married and unemployed son seeks an independent business while the landlord lacks another suitable shop for him, the landlord’s personal need is bona fide.

issues.legal_issue: Comparative hardship must be assessed by weighing the tenant’s length of occupancy against the availability of suitable alternative premises and the landlord’s own need, rather than treating long occupancy as decisive.
material_facts: The tenant’s family had occupied the disputed shop for a long period.
The tenant had another shop available in which he could shift his business; the sale deed established that the property he had purchased included a shop.
The tenant had previously conducted his own business from another shop and had established his son in that shop.
The landlady had no other shop in which to establish her married and unemployed son.
There was no evidence that the landlady’s husband’s existing business was so extensive as to weigh against release under the relevant factor in Rule 16(2).
issues.conclusion: Comparative hardship favored the landlady; the tenant’s long occupancy did not outweigh the availability of another shop to him and the landlady’s lack of another shop for her son.
issues.legal_principle: The fourth proviso to Section 21(1) requires consideration of likely hardship to the tenant from granting release as against likely hardship to the landlord from refusing it. Rule 16(2)(a)–(c) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Rules, 1972 identifies relevant factors for business premises: longer occupancy weighs against release, suitable alternative accommodation for the tenant weighs in favor of release, and the extent of the landlord’s existing business may also matter. Length of tenancy is one factor, not the sole criterion; availability of suitable alternative accommodation to the tenant can neutralize its weight. No earlier cases were relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_release_proceeding and tenant_long_occupancy and tenant_has_suitable_alternative_shop and landlord_lacks_other_suitable_shop and landlord_existing_business_not_extensive

predicates.tenant_eviction_release_proceeding: A landlord seeks release of business premises occupied by a tenant.
predicates.tenant_long_occupancy: The tenant or the tenant’s predecessor has occupied the premises for a long period.
predicates.tenant_has_suitable_alternative_shop: The tenant has another suitable shop available to which the business can be shifted.
predicates.landlord_lacks_other_suitable_shop: The landlord has no other suitable shop for the proposed use.
predicates.landlord_existing_business_not_extensive: The landlord’s existing business is not shown to be so extensive as to weigh against release.
predicates.comparative_hardship_favors_landlord: The hardship from refusing release to the landlord outweighs the hardship from granting release to the tenant.

issues.definition: In a tenant-eviction release proceeding, where the tenant has occupied the premises for a long period but has a suitable alternative shop, the landlord lacks another suitable shop, and the landlord’s existing business is not extensive, comparative hardship favors the landlord.
